title: Some styles are implemented as UA rules instead of presentational hints
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard? https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/rendering.html has lots of styles which are "[expected](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/rendering.html#expected) to apply, as [presentational hints](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/rendering.html#presentational-hints)". For example, from https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/rendering.html#tables-2 ```css table[border] > tr > td, table[border] > tr > th, table[border] > thead > tr > td, table[border] > thead > tr > th, table[border] > tbody > tr > td, table[border] > tbody > tr > th, table[border] > tfoot > tr > td, table[border] > tfoot > tr > th { /* only if border is not equivalent to zero */ border-width: 1px; border-style: inset; } ``` No browser implements this as a presentational hint, they do it using the UA origin. The difference is observable: ```html
``` You can still see `border-style: inset` in Firefox, Chrome and Safari, because it's in the UA origin. If it was a presentational hint, it would have been reverted, according to https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade-5/#preshint This other example is an actual presentational hint: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/rendering.html#flow-content-3 ```css pre[wrap] { white-space: pre-wrap; } ``` as observed in this testcase, which outputs `pre`, because `white-space: pre-wrap` gets reverted since it's an actual presentational hint. ```html 


```

I think all the styles need to be reviewed one by one, check what browsers do, and update the spec accordingly
